column3: Near parallel: warning, personal liability, and no protector or intercessor besides God.
Supplies the day of individual recompense that gives the warning its judicial horizon.
Confirms that every route through death ends in gathering to God.
Clarifies reminder as a means toward taqwa without assuming another's account.
Its immediate context separates people from one another's accounts and forbids exclusion.
Shows feared future vulnerability becoming present taqwa and responsible speech.
Contrasts reliance on the Lord with an opposing claim of operative authority.
Its immediate context limits the messenger to following revealed warning, not hidden power.
Frames warning as concern for a people before a grave day of punishment.
Affirms sole divine judgment and no protector besides Him.
Shows harmful authority becoming effective through accepted patronage and association.
Directly joins a received reminder, warning, taqwa, and mercy.
Adds fear expressed through compliance, without the gathering or intercession frame.
Crisis exposes exclusive calling on God, sharpening the denial of alternative support.
Closely repeats the exclusion of both protector and intercessor under divine rule.
Places warning before an imminent day where no effective intercessor is obeyed.
Shows distress turning invocation exclusively to God and displacing associations.
Tests a claimed special divine closeness, but only indirectly bears on final support.
Explains varied warning as ordered toward taqwa and renewed remembrance.
Extends the taqwa response, though it adds little to the warning and gathering frame.
Denies that acquisitions or chosen allies can shield against the coming punishment.
Associates an unbent Qur'anic address with taqwa, supplementing warning's function.
Continues the nearby refusal to direct devotion toward those besides God.
States dispersal on earth and the decisive gathering to Him with unusual economy.
Names a distorted fear of divine and messenger judgment rather than receptive fear.
Shows delayed acknowledgment of wrongdoing when punishment arrives.
Qualifies any beneficial intercession as dependent on divine permission.
Links worship without authority or knowledge to the absence of a helper for wrongdoers.
Shows resistant perception, but does not materially clarify the warning's stated outcome.
Uses lack of taqwa to explain repeated covenant breaking in a different setting.
Identifies failure to fear the Hereafter as what blocks warning from taking effect.
Adds universal questioning of recipients and messengers to the accountability horizon.
Boundary evidence: turning away from a covenant marks loss of its protective relation.
Confirms that a human recipient of revelation is charged to warn people.
Defines messengers as warners and ties reception to freedom from fear and grief.
Combines taqwa with gathering to God, though within a specific social command.
Broadens gathering to all communities of creatures before their Lord.
Punitive destination alone adds no distinct route to the focus reading.
Directly contests the claimed intercessory status of those invoked besides God.
Reiterates that no protector or helper exists besides God under His life-and-death rule.
Sets a point when later belief or earned good no longer benefits, heightening warning's urgency.
Provides a qualified divine closeness with no fear, a useful counterpoint to illicit patronage.
Limits intercession to those connected with truth and knowledge.
Its punishment image does not add a distinct interpretive element.
Repeats lack of protector and helper without the focus's gathering or intercession detail.
Food imagery has no meaningful bearing on the focus.
Contrasts worldly diversion with the better final abode for those who practice taqwa.
Denies partner-based intercessors, while preserving the contrast route as a boundary.
Reaffirms exclusive divine dominion and absence of any other protector or helper.
Portrays the day of flight with no defender against God.
Its retrospective formula preserves warning and consequence, but is less specific than later evidence.
Narrows the warning task first to the nearest kin.
Shows that even overwhelming signs and gathering would not compel receptive belief.
Offers only a minimal pairing of giving with taqwa.
Shows fear yielding to trust and decisive action rather than paralysis.
Affirms resurrection as a binding divine promise, grounding the gathering horizon.
Sets communal taqwa boundaries; the contrast link remains boundary rather than support.
Denies that beings invoked besides God can remove or redirect harm.
Contrasts fear of associations with fear directed toward the Lord's will and knowledge.
Questions whether those besides God can give aid or defend themselves.
Combines no protectors besides God with a humiliating eschatological gathering.
Uses material protections as a distant analogy for the focus's protective concern.
Uses fear for a people to invoke prior collective days of consequence.
Simply and explicitly assigns universal gathering to the wise, knowing Lord.
Frames choosing a protector as exclusive devotion to the Creator and sustainer.
Contrast evidence around commitment and fear of death, not a positive route to the focus.
Defines divine boundaries as a discipline ordered toward taqwa.
Gives a stark direct warning of a blazing fire, though it is otherwise sparse.
Makes warning present the later plea for delay before that plea is too late.
Connects messengers' recitation with taqwa, reform, and release from fear and grief.
Its account of loyalty and resolve does not clarify the focus's warning or final support.
Rejects an alternative divine claim through punishment, only indirectly relevant.
Links detailed guidance and mercy with belief in meeting the Lord.
Earthly coercive mustering is a contrary model of gathering, not final gathering.
In the same surah joins taqwa and worship with the unavoidable gathering to Him.
Affirms that warners were sent within earlier communities.
Shows mercy's realized allotment joined to taqwa, giving the response a positive horizon.
Distinguishes preventive taqwa and forgiveness while locating both with God.
Subordinates intercession to divine permission within comprehensive divine governance.
Records a demand for a second visible warner, a limited boundary on warning reception.
Links return to God with disclosure of deeds while regulating competing loyalties.
Uses a realized punishment as renewed evidence of the force of prior warnings.
Applies taqwa to contractual accuracy, far from the focus's eschatological warning.
Adds an apocalyptic image of creatures being gathered, though not the focus's relational judgment.
Provides a coercive human gathering that serves only as a contrary comparison.
Joins a legal command and taqwa to gathering, but with little further illumination.
Concentrates the messenger's role in the single term: warner.
In the same surah, gathering exposes alleged partners for direct challenge.
Shows the invoked themselves seeking nearness, mercy, and fearing punishment.
Depicts situational fear and watchfulness rather than the focus's anticipatory warning.
Makes an enduring sign legible to those who fear painful punishment.
Reiterates that wrongdoers have neither protector nor helper, despite being a tail-audit item.
Reiterates the paired absence of protector and helper besides God.
Personal fear reassured in a narrative scene does not clarify the warning's ethical function.
Moves from acknowledgment of divine governance to the demand for taqwa.
Denies any shield from God amid worldly and final punishment.
Places every self's earning under divine watch while challenging alleged partners.
Offers inward fearful remembrance as a sustaining practice, but not the final-account frame.
Pairs taqwa with obedience in a bare repeated exhortation.
Combines filial warning of punishment with the danger of becoming a patron of Satan.
Adds the individual day in which compensation and intercession do not avail.
Reiterates personal recompense and the failure of ransom and intercession.
Places intercession outside ordinary exchange, friendship, and payment.
Defines intercession as possible only by divine leave under total divine sovereignty.
Contrasts God's guardianship with competing guardianships that lead away from light.
Supplies return to God and full repayment for every self's earning.
Shows fear being redirected from Satanic allies toward God.
Names God as sufficient protector and helper amid hostile loyalties.
Contrasts those aligned with God and with false powers in a conflict setting.
Excludes substitute protector or helper for wrongdoing before God.
Joins refusal with the absence of any protector or helper besides God.
Presents attachment to God as entry into mercy and guidance, a secondary patronage contrast.
Positively identifies God's guardianship and the believing community's aligned loyalty.
Regulates whom believers take as allies, clarifying the relational stakes of wali language.
Denies helpers to those who associate others with God.
Places people before their Lord and exposes denial of the encounter.
Portrays return to God one by one, with claimed intercessors absent.
Adds a comprehensive gathering of humans and jinn with accountable dialogue.
Connects messengers' warnings with meeting the day and self-witnessed liability.
Makes each self bear its own burden before final return and disclosure.
Records the belated search for intercessors when the final outcome arrives.
Denies that those invoked besides God can help their callers or themselves.
Bounds even repeated pleas for forgiveness by divine judgment.
Restricts funeral prayer over a rejected group, a narrow boundary around advocacy.
Gathers all, then separates those who associated partners from their claimed partners.
Makes every self test what it sent ahead and return to its true master.
Denies independent power to remove harm or confer benefit to those besides God.
Shows followed leaders disclaiming power to relieve their followers at the final confrontation.
Has Satan disclaim coercive authority and shift responsibility back to those who answered him.
Challenges taking divine servants as guardians besides God.
Limits intercession to one holding a covenant with the Most Merciful.
States that all come to God individually.
Limits intercession on that day to permission and accepted speech.
Makes intercession contingent on divine approval and depicts fear before God.
Shows final gathering severing ordinary lineage claims and mutual questioning.
Disavows taking protectors besides God and ties the error to heedlessness.
Denies any protector or helper against God's intended harm or mercy.
Removes independent power, partnership, and supporting role from those besides God.
Reasserts that no bearer carries another's burden, even when help is sought.
Directly denies that other intercessors can avail against the Most Merciful.
States that all are brought together before God.
Depicts a single summons after which all are presented before the Lord.
Assigns all intercession exclusively to God before return to Him.
Orders turning and submission before punishment arrives beyond help.
Offers the positive opposite: no fear or grief for a divinely addressed group.
Makes Qur'anic warning specifically address those who fear the threatened outcome.
Limits even angelic intercession to divine permission and approval.
Denies refuge or shelter from God apart from Him.
Restricts speech and intercession-like address to divine permission and truth.
